newsitem.title: UK: Remote British islands won't vote in election.
newsitem.headline: Remote British islands won't vote in election.

text.p: The most remote community in the British Isles will not vote in the May 1 general election, as none of the 29 adults on the Atlantic islands of St Kilda have bothered to sign up to the electoral register.

This saves Western Isles council the expense of a polling station in the islands, 110 miles (175 km) west of the Scottish mainland, and the 5,000 pound ($8,000) cost of a helicopter to fly ballot boxes to and fro.
Council officials said the inhabitants of the island were simply not interested enough in the election to register.
"Fortunately, nobody has registered," said one. "It's a bit of a relief."
Twenty-two of the 29 run a missile-tracking station. Six study sheep and the other is warden of a bird sanctuary.
The five islands in the St Kilda group were inhabited for more than 2,000 years, but poverty and famine led drove the d the last 40 native islanders away in 1930.
Western Isles is a marginal constituency where the Scottish National Party candidate, popular Gaelic singer Anne Lorne Gillies, is fighting to oust Labour member Calum MacDonald. ($1=.6161 Pound)
